script.base: San Francisco is a 7-point home favorite in a 51.5 total, so the book expects the 49ers to lead and both teams to score (SF 29.2, Washington 22.2). Base script: Brock Purdy attacks early because Washington blitzes 46 percent and SF EPA per dropback vs blitz is +0.70, with George Kittle working the middle where Washington allows 10.15 YPA, then Christian McCaffrey (41 carries, 195 rush yards over weeks 3-5) closes the game on the ground against a Washington run defense allowing 4.13 YPC and 11 runs of 10-plus. Washington, without Jacory Croskey-Merritt (out, 39 carries and 133 yards in that same window), falls behind and throws more with Jayden Daniels.
script.flip1: Washington hangs around or leads. Nick Bosa is out and Mykel Williams and Gracen Halton are questionable, so the 49ers' pass rush is thin, Daniels can extend plays (last4 rush games 31, 69, 104), SF never gets the late clock-kill, and McCaffrey's rushing line stalls while both passing games stay live.
script.flip2: San Francisco blows it open early. Starters sit in the fourth quarter, Kittle and McCaffrey lose late snaps, Washington abandons the run completely, and garbage-time yards go to Commanders depth receivers rather than Rachaad White or Austin Ekeler rushing lines.

injury_fallout: Source is the pack official pre-game nflverse injury report only. Final inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff are not in the pack, so every Questionable tag is unresolved. Confirmed out, Washington: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) removes the lead back, so Rachaad White (15 carries, 53 yards L3) and Austin Ekeler (7 carries, 28 yards L3) absorb carries and Croskey-Merritt's 5 targets and 42 receiving yards; Jeremy McNichols is only Questionable (quad) and is not assumed active. Marcus Mariota (knee) out leaves Daniels as the quarterback. Charles Omenihu (groin) out and Javon Kinlaw (ankle) questionable thin the Washington defensive front McCaffrey runs at. Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) out and Jordan Magee (hamstring) questionable remove linebackers, which helps the 49ers' tight end and running back in the short middle. Nick Cross, Percy Butler and Tyler Owens are questionable safeties and Trey Amos is a questionable corner, so the Washington secondary is not confirmed healthy. Lucas Patrick (guard, illness) questionable: if he sits, Washington pressure rate rises, rushing efficiency falls, and quick throws to Ekeler and Chig Okonkwo rise. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) questionable on 16 targets and 68 yards L3: if he is limited, Antonio Williams, Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks and Okonkwo gain targets. Confirmed out, San Francisco: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) removes 9 targets, 47 receiving yards and 7 carries for 62 yards, which consolidates to Kittle, McCaffrey, Mike Evans if active, and depth wideouts Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. Nick Bosa (knee) out, plus Mykel Williams (knee) and Gracen Halton (quad) questionable, cuts the 49ers' pass rush. Marques Sigle (ankle) out, Siran Neal (neck) questionable and Upton Stout (shoulder) questionable thin the secondary Washington throws at. Garret Wallow (hamstring) out is a linebacker absence on the SF side. Mike Evans (ribs) and Christian Kirk (calf) are questionable, so the 49ers' receiver room may be Deebo-out plus two game-time decisions; do not treat Evans as inactive.

matchup.shell: No middle-of-field open versus closed chart and no man versus zone rate are in the pack, so the shell is unknown and is not invented. What is known is location YPA and blitz rate.
matchup.pressure: San Francisco blitzes 31 percent. Washington EPA per dropback is -0.20 versus the blitz and +0.17 with no blitz, so pressure kills Commanders efficiency and deep wideout yards and should funnel checkdowns. Washington blitzes 46 percent. San Francisco EPA per dropback is +0.70 versus the blitz and +0.29 clean, so the 49ers want Washington to blitz and can answer with Kittle in the middle and McCaffrey on checkdowns. Bosa being out does not change Washington's blitz rate; it changes how often San Francisco can pressure Daniels.
matchup.bleeds: Washington defense over 5 games: rush 4.13 yards per carry and 11 runs of 10-plus; 16 passes of 20-plus for 199 yards; YPA left 4.82 on 65 attempts, middle 10.15 on 40 attempts, right 7.35 on 85 attempts. The bleed is the middle, then the right side, then the run. San Francisco defense over 5 games is the opposite on the ground: 3.70 yards per carry and only 4 runs of 10-plus, with compressed pass YPA (left 6.38 on 68, middle 6.0 on 17, right 5.89 on 88) and only 9 passes of 20-plus for 184 yards.
matchup.overlap: The core overlap is George Kittle, 19 targets, 176 yards and 125 air yards over weeks 3-5, into Washington's middle (10.15 YPA) and into a 46 percent blitz that San Francisco has destroyed (+0.70 EPA). Second overlap is Christian McCaffrey's 41 carries into a 4.13 YPC run defense in a lead script. Washington's deep group (Williams 168 air yards, Burks 159, Deebo Brown 155, McLaurin 148) would want Sigle out, but that is not the same overlap: San Francisco has allowed few explosives and Washington is worse when blitzed.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both legs lost. Kittle finished under 67.5 because Mike Evans played through the ribs and kept a 24-target share, San Francisco led by two scores at half, and Washington stopped blitzing so the middle never opened; the 24-yard game in the last4 log is the template, not the 80 and 82. McCaffrey finished under 63.5 because Washington jumped ahead, Brock Purdy's 74 rush yards in the L3 window and Keaton Black's 16 carries took the rushing production, and a late lead still was not 15 efficient carries once Washington stacked the box. That counter-case is why the card is flagged and not bet. It is not stronger than the middle-bleed plus blitz-EPA overlap, so the Kittle read is not dropped. The McCaffrey counter-case is strong enough to keep him a lean rather than a strong.
slip_story: One WAS@SF story only: San Francisco control game, lead, throw into Washington's middle and blitz to score the 29.2 implied total, then hand the ball to McCaffrey against a 4.13 YPC run defense. The two-leg slip is Kittle receiving yards over 67.5 with McCaffrey rushing yards over 63.5. They win together if the game follows the base script and does not become a first-half blowout. Do not add Washington rushing overs for White or Ekeler; those need Washington to stay on schedule on the ground, which the dog script rejects even after Croskey-Merritt was ruled out. Do not add a game under; 51.5 and these overs need points. Do not add depth wideout overs for Cowing, Cooks, Watkins or Burks. Burks at 7.5 versus logs of 13, 47 and 26 is a lagging number, but he is a 159-air-yard shot into a 31 percent San Francisco blitz that already makes Washington EPA negative, so averages alone do not make that leg. No touchdown legs. One market per player. Weather is unknown, so this is not a wind or rain stack.
